title: The memory palace (method of loci): its legend, how memory champions use it, and what brain studies found

sources.title: Use this ancient technique to remember (almost) anything
Ancient Brain Training Technique Can Boost Memory
Memorization tool bulks up brain’s internal connections, scientists say
Routes to remembering: the brains behind superior memory
sources.note: 只取摘要的結論（另見 PubMed 12483214）

facts.text: Competitors at memory championships use variations of the method of loci, also called the memory palace.
The method links each item to a vivid image placed at a spot along a familiar route, which is later walked again in the mind.
Odd, shocking or unusual images are recommended because they are easier to recall.
Legend credits the Greek poet Simonides with the method: after a banquet hall collapsed, he identified the victims by recalling where each had sat.
The method dates back more than two millennia; Simonides lived in the fifth century BC.
A 2003 study found that people with superior memory did not differ from others in intellectual ability or brain structure.
While memorizing, they used a spatial strategy that engaged brain regions important for spatial memory and navigation.
In a 2017 study, people who completed six weeks of daily method-of-loci training recalled almost as many words as memory athletes.
Four months after the training ended, the trained group still achieved similar results.
After training, their brain connectivity patterns became more similar to those of memory athletes.
